data.body:
RCA (Phase 1, proven at runtime).

Mechanism confirmed by reproduction in a --filter=blob:none clone whose origin.fetch maps all heads (+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*), with a small 'main' and a large unrelated 'tickets' branch:

  rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.resolve_ref('origin/main', ..., blobless=False) issued exactly:
    git -c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=10 fetch --quiet --no-filter origin
  i.e. NO refspec -> git applies the configured origin.fetch and transfers EVERY head. After the call, origin/tickets (the large unrelated branch, never requested) was present locally. This is the broad-fetch that made a post-merge review-plan spend 512s and time out git fetch at 300s while only a code SHA was needed.

Root cause: resolve_ref()'s FIRST fetch (repo_snapshot.py line ~265) calls fetch_origin() with no ref, so the network fetch is unscoped. fetch_origin already supports a targeted ref; only the caller was unscoped. The targeted fallback (line ~270) fires only when the broad fetch fails to resolve, so in the common origin/main case the broad fetch always runs first.

Defect origin (caused_by): story hoot-glove-foyer (6d56-8c12-9953-4d25), 'Faithful, lock-free snapshot materialization core' (shipped in b25fafc, epic raze-vet-ditch). Its plan specified 'Coalesced git fetch origin ... resolve ref' — the broad, unscoped fetch by design. Hence class plan_defect: latent since introduction, surfaced under partial/promisor clone + a huge tickets branch. Distinct from strained-bare-turnstone (transport stalls / voting) and grassy-cracked-morpho (completion close scanning).

Fix (Phase 2): scope resolve_ref's first fetch to the requested ref — for a <remote>/<name> ref fetch '+<name>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<name>' (updates the tracking ref, transfers only that branch); otherwise pass the ref as a targeted want. Preserve blobless policy, remote-ref support, and fail-closed semantics; keep the SHA-want fallback. RED regression test pins the scoped fetch argv and rejects an unscoped no-filter origin fetch.
